Qerovot for Shabbat Tequmah (the Sabbath between Yom haShoah and Yom ha-Atsma'ut), by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Qerovot for Shabbat Tequmah (the Sabbath between Yom haShoah and Yom ha-Atsma'ut), by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: Blessed are You,
o Cause, our God
and God of our ancestors.
God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob.
The Deity,
great and mighty and awesome;
the almighty Deity,
who well repays kindness,
and possesses all,
and remembers the kindnesses of ancestors
and sends a redeemer to their descendants
for Their Name’s sake,
in love.
Sovereign, Help
and Rescue and Shield —
Reshut
With the permission of Yah, seated in holiness,
and by the knowledge of the righteous interpreters of Zion,
I ask for grace, mercy from all the elders,
to establish reading qerovot and to publicize new takes.
Magen
Days of devastation afflicted the Daughter,
and a time of struggle for the one preserved like a pupil.
Where is anything like it? To the fire from the frying pan;
the land waited and rested its sabbath.
“Hear, Israel!” cried the people,
and prayed that You would hear the cry of the people.
“I will shatter the yoke,” You said sweetly.
Ah, where is the shoot coming out from their stump?
The guardians of the Dove, the partisans,
stood to shield the children of the Sleepers.
The daughter of ‘Amaleq, the oppressor, could not defeat the nobles.
Her wickedness was revealed and judgments were ordained.

tei:l.tei:note: In most modern Ashkenazi practice, the catenae of verses inserted after the first three piyyutim are not recited.

tei:lg.tei:l: As it is written:
Then the land will desire its sabbaths
all the days of desolation,
you in the land of your enemies;
then the land will rest
and desire its sabbaths. (Leviticus 26:34)
And it is said:
But even then, when they are in their enemies’ land,
I will not spurn nor repel them to destroy them,
to void My covenant with them,
for I the Cause am their God. (Leviticus 26:44)
And it is said:
And you will remember all the path
that the Cause your God walked you
these forty years in the desert,
so as to afflict you to test you
to know if in your hearts
you will keep Their commandments
or not. (Deuteronomy 8:2)
And it is said:
And we cried to the Cause God of our ancestors,
and the Cause heard our voices
and saw our affliction
and our toils and our oppression. (Deuteronomy 26:7)
And it is said:
And a branch will grow from Jesse’s stump,
and a twig will flower from his roots. (Isaiah 11:1)
And it is said:
Ah, great is that day, where is one like it?
And it is a time of stress for Jacob,
and from it he will be saved. (Jeremiah 30:7)
And it is said:
And on that day — declare the Cause of Forces —
I will shatter his yoke from upon your neck,
and your bonds I will break,
and no more will they serve strangers. (Jeremiah 30:8)
And it is said:
The Cause’s mercies have not ceased;
nor are Their compassions ended. (Lamentations 3:22)
And it is said:
Ended are your iniquities, fair Zion,
no more will you be exiled.
Recalled are your iniquities, fair Edom,
uncovered are all your sins. (Lamentations 4:22)
And it is said:
Those sowing in tears
will in cheer reap. (Psalms 126:5)
And it is said:
Often have they assailed me since youth,
but they have not done defeat to me. (Psalms 129:1)
To me is Yah lover, upon me is Their desire.
Screamed I, They heard in Their great compassion.
As Their mercy is boundless, allow me to praise Them.
Covering, Israel’s Holiness shields with Their defense!
Blessed are You, o Cause, shield of Abraham.
You are mighty forever, Master,
You bring life to the dead,
greatly saving.
You send down the dew.
You provide for life in kindness,
reviving the dead in great mercy,
lift the fallen,
heal the sick,
free the bound,
and keep faith with sleepers in the dust.
Who is like You, Master of Powerful Acts,
and who can be compared to You?
Sovereign, who brings death and life
and causes salvation to sprout.
And trusted are You to revive the dead —
Meḥayeh
The ancestral covenant You remembered;
the first father who You converted,
the unique one whose slaughter You stopped,
and the pure one who You took as firstborn over the firstborn.
“Of our foes, do not fear,” You commanded.
Did You not take us out of Egypt?
Remember the martyrs if You are angered at us;
pray let the blood of the slaughtered with us be avenged!
Give all our despoilers to the plunder;
the chiefs of our enemies to defeat.
And for the sake of the betrothed nation,
the desert will be made green, that we may be assembled.
As it is written:
And I will remember My covenant with Jacob,
as well as My covenant with Isaac,
as well as My covenant with Abraham I will remember,
and the land I will remember. (Leviticus 26:42)
And it is said:
Do not fear them;
remember, yes, remember
what the Cause your God did
to Pharaoh and all Egypt. (Deuteronomy 7:18)
And it is said:
And the Cause took us out from Egypt
with a strong hand
and an outstretched arm
and great awe
and signs
and wonders. (Deuteronomy 26:8)
And it is said:
And you will say on that day,
“I give thanks to You, Cause,
for You were angered at me,
but Your wrath turned back
and You comforted me.” (Isaiah 12:1)
And it is said:
Thus, all who would devour you will be devoured,
and all who would stress you will all go in capitivity,
and your despoilers will be for the spoil,
and all your plunderers I will give to plunder. (Jeremiah 30:16)
And it is said:
Return, Cause, all our captivity,
like wadis in the Negev. (Psalms 126:4)
And it is said:
In God we will do might,
and They will defeat our foes. (Psalms 108:14)
Our foes indeed rise up to destroy us,
Stressors of the community to exile us.
Allow us to fight for our lives,
And let dew of might come upon our nation.
Blessed are You, o Cause, who revives the dead.
Meshalesh
Vines to plant in the hills of Samaria,
from the Jordan valley to the Sharon plain.
Israel returned in hope to the stronghold,
and crossed over the water like those carrying the ark.
A good province it is, how beautiful to the eyes!
They looked down from Their abode and gave it to us in life —
wells and aquifers flowing milk and honey like water;
Zion, doubled joy of all the earth!
The king, sweet singer of Israel,
said ascents by the short name of the Redeemer.
And as dreamers we will hear “Go to the house of the Deity!”
Return Your presence to dwelling in Ariel!
As it is written:
Again you will plant vineyards
in the hills of Samaria;
plantings planted and fruiting. (Jeremiah 31:5)
And it is said:
Return to the stronghold, prisoners of hope!
This very day a doubled promise I will return to you. (Zechariah 9:12)
And it is said:
And when the soles of the feet of the priests
bearing the ark of the Cause, Master of all the earth,
rest in the waters of the Jordan,
the waters of the Jordan will be cut off —
the waters flowing down —
and stand up in one pile. (Joshua 3:13)
And it is said:
For the Cause your God is bringing you to a good land,
a land of rivers of water, wellsprings, and aquifers
going out in the valley and the mountain. (Deuteronomy 8:7)
And it is said:
Look down from Your holy abode, from heaven,
and bless Your people Israel
and the land that You gave us,
as You swore to our ancestors,
a land flowing with milk and honey. (Deuteronomy 26:15)
And it is said:
Beautiful sight, joy of all the earth,
Mount Zion,
the utmost mountainous-north,
the city of the great Sovereign. (Psalms 48:3)
And it is said:
Rather, rejoice and cheer forever, as I created,
for behold I am creating with Jerusalem cheer
and her people joy. (Isaiah 65:18)
And it is said:
A song of ascents, of David.
I rejoiced on their saying to me,
“let us go to the Cause’s house!” (Psalms 122:1)
And it is said:
A song of ascents.
On the Cause’s returning the exiles of Zion,
we would be like dreamers. (Psalms 126:1)
And it is said:
For the Cause chose Zion;
They desired for it as a dwelling. (Psalms 132:13)
For it, Israel and Judah will be gathered to Them;
So rejoice and cheer in song and thanksgiving,
And return to your land, as no longer a wanderer.
Collecting us from the predator’s hand, the Holy One!
As it is written:
And They will raise a flag to the nations
and gather the banished of Israel,
and the scattered of Judah They will gather
from the four corners of the earth. (Isaiah 11:12)
And it is said:
Rejoice and cheer, dweller in Zion,
for great in your midst is Israel’s Holy One! (Isaiah 12:6)
And it is said:
Thus said the Cause:
behold I return the exile of the tents of Jacob,
and will have compassion on his dwellings,
and the city will be built on its ruin,
and the palace on its justice will sit. (Jeremiah 30:18)
And it is said:
And his leader will be from him,
and his ruler will come out from his midst,
and I will bring him near,
and he will be close to Me,
for who could pledge his heart to be close to Me? —
declares the Cause. (Jeremiah 30:21)
And it is said:
The Cause reigns forever;
your God, Zion, from generation to generation;
praise Yah! (Psalms 146:10)
And You are holy,
enthroned on Israel’s praise. (Psalms 22:4)
El Na
Deity, please!
From calamity and destruction, from among the stresses,
I strengthen my hands and lift my head.
Two thousand years full of bitter days
passed from the start to these things.
The arrogant strangers laughed at us, mocked us,
the marshals and officials and tyrants and princes.
We asked in sorrow before the stressors,
“how can we sing of You songs in a foreign land?”
Nevertheless, despite all these pains,
we did not despair, but awaited evenings and mornings
to build new the ruins of the cities,
to skip over the hills, leap over the mountains.
In the lands of the Hagrites
and the countries of the Nazarenes,
we were dwelling,
and we were aliens,
lacking from our land,
until the time came, the era of loving returning.
Ḥai v-Qayyam
Living and enduring,
awesome and exalted and holy!
Old and new the double-settlements
hoped a hope of two thousand years;
Zion and Jerusalem
the goal of the double-exiles.
New and old the land,
wrote the mountain, shadow of wisdom.
Kishinev he saw in turmoil,
ruined like a battlefield.
He wrote, “Where is their security?
Were you sold, as said, for free?”
First to Zion, there they are,
and Jerusalem for their sake.
To Basel the elders went,
to the committee of Zionists,
to say: there is no city to which they face
other than where the children of David encamp.
Mountains in the end erode too,
and giants also pass on.
The founder’s days ended,
but what he founded survived him.
The mountain-shadow is in the shadow of his mountain.
His name it took to honor him.
He was buried a century after his generation,
there, on his name, to honor his memory.
Deity, please,
forever are You adored
and forever are You sanctified
and forever and aye will You reign and be exalted,
the Deity,
sovereign, awesome, high and holy,
for You are the Sovereign,
Sovereign of sovereigns,
whose sovereignty is eternal;
tell Their awesomenesses,
recount Their strength,
glorify Their forces,
sanctify Them,
exalt Them,
cheer, song, and laudation,
mighty praises of Their glory.
Qiqlar
Indeed there is a flowing land,
sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land our ancestors,
by whose seed the nations were blessed, walked.
They tread round its borders.
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land of grain and wine,
myrtle flourishing with cypress,
roses, myrrh, and chief spices.
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land flowing with honey of dates —
but the flint-rock is also the honeycomb of bees,
the impure producing pure.
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
The land of Israel, an eternal inheritance!
All who shame her will be shamed.
The legion that sought to conquer her vanished.
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land of water of four rivers,
fish and seafood in the seven seas,
saupes and Eilat-fish to satiation.
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land above all lands in our eyes,
fruitful with vineyards of our vines.
Rejoicing, let us rejoice in drinking our wines!
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land holy and blessed.
Content and valued is the foot
that steps in its borders!
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
A land of Teaching and wisdom.
You will rise, do its restoration,
on the sabbath that we have called “revival!”
Indeed there is a flowing land, sequestered for the pupil;
and its law is to attend the Sabbath,
consecrated!
Reshut
And thus, the city will be built on its ruin... (Jeremiah 30:18)
Although these days are new,
By comparison to the antiquity of the holy seasons,
Granted, these days too are important and necessary,
By permission of the decreers of law and custom and elders.
Espy a precedent for the third,
Whereas all the people accepted it, not just individuals!
Zealously they accepted my sanctuary’s rededication,
From the teaching of the Hasmoneans in my holy house.
Traditions like this were established before us by
Just ones of the people, our law’s interpreters.
Consider local Purim days in our foundations,
As the law of learned Saragossans in our memory.
Monarchies in which we dwelt,
Norm among us to celebrate among them.
Spanish Jews would praise on their thanksgiving days,
By reasoning of the obelisks of their synagogue-boards.
Pronouncing with my throat, I laid out
Challenge and thanksgiving and remembrance.
Quite near to before the ark I came,
In the cousel of the Rudiment and Ultimate,
Sharing a rolled-up song I composed,
This people’s might in cheer.
Strengthen me, please, all the community,
In reading the azhara of independence like in the scroll.
Azharah
The land of Israel is the place fair Judah was established.
In it her unique form in spirit, faith, and politics was crafted.
Cultural treasures for every nation formed by her hand,
Such as the Biblical wisdom that all the world honors.
Judah was exiled from his land with a strong arm.
But yet he kept his faith in distant scattering.
He remembered in prayer and hoped in stress and distress:
Renew freedom in my land, return my holding!
Before this era this traditional connection endured.
Jews of each generation strove to return to the land quickly.
In this time, they returned in droves, rank and file,
To hold onto their birthplace, the place the people was born.
Defiant immigrants and guardians and pioneers returned.
They made wastes bloom and spoke the Hebrew tongue.
They organized cities and towns and grew the settlement.
Look, they incubated their own economy and culture.
Those who rose to the land, pursuing its peace, ordered
armies to defend, lest war break out.
They brought progress’s blessing close to its inhabitants;
their desire to achieve awesome independence.
The year of the count of “announcing truth,”
All in the congress heard as he raised his voice,
Theodor Herzl, and announced in words:
“Our revival we will merit! Open for us the gates!”
Support for this right was found in the declaration
That Balfour declared in the year 5678 of the count.
The mandate government confirmed this right:
People and land linked truly in tradition.
Pain and destruction befell our people.
The flowers of Jeshurun were given to the slaughter.
My mockers acted and millions passed on;
Dangers against us were made known in the nations’ eyes.
It was clearly visible that a solution was needed:
The homeland of Jeshurun from where it was expelled,
to renew there a state for the poor and needy people,
like a people among nations, not to be uprooted.
Jews of the slaughter’s remnant and others on earth
Were moved to ascend to the house of the hall.
Stopping, hardship, and danger moved them not from the ladder.
They claimed the right to freedom and honorable labor.
And in the second war in which all nations fought,
The Hebrew settlement rose in the just battle.
Their soldiers’ blood was spilt and flowed.
Our recompense: be counted in the established peoples.
In the month of Kislev on the sixteenth day,
In the year of return by our count, it’s good for all flesh,
The United Nations swore a binding-oath:
The land of Israel would be handed over to its people.
The settlement should perform — claimed the assembly —
required steps to plant the treetop.
It is an unchanging law to be kept,
Established and irrevocable is the letter.
This is a natural right for us, on account of
the right to stand for ourselves, like every nation.
No difference, no change, the gold is not dimmed.
Thus, we the fellows of the people’s council, are gathered,
on the day the British Mandate ends —
Representatives of the existing Hebrew settlement,
Along with the Zionist movement that will remain,
By force of our right that will never end,
the natural right in our hands to redeem,
the declaration of the United Nations assembly —
We announce, to establish with acknowledgements
The state of Israel in these fields!
We decree that starting from this night,
The sixth of Iyyar, May to the nations of the diaspora,
The council heads will temporarily act as a government;
The nation will soon choose its own leadership.
So as to gather the diaspora, open will be
The state for Jewish aliyah in safety.
Pleasant will be the land, that there be success for us,
And for all its inhabitants, not a young woman forgotten.
Its foundations: freedom and righteousness and peace,
By the prophetic vision, more precious than diamond,
To establish total equality as befitting all its citizens —
Race and sex, faith and conscience, language and education and culture, this is no dream!
Guarding all holy places,
The purities of all faiths in mortal hearts,
And being faithful to the elucidated principles
written in the UN charter for those seeking them out.
The state desires to cooperate
with UN institutions and representatives under its flag,
from the day of its proclamation, to do work,
Working to establish land-unity in the matter of economy.
To the nations we call to lend a hand to build our state,
To accept Israel to the family of peoples, our community.
Amid this bloody attack we call in earnest:
Ishmael, to receive in peace his portion in our citizenship.
In peace and good neighborliness we reach out
a hand to all our neighbor-states, peoples and leaders.
Our border is here, just as with our tribal ancestors.
It’s desireable to cooperate in general and particular!
To contribute its portion in effort, Israel is prepared.
In this region we will work progress — aren’t we here too?
See, sons of the dove, that the bird too found a nest!
And thus, stand in ranks for the redemption of the dwelling!
Registered out of trust in the Rock of Israel,
Here we are witnessing in this declaration to be redeemed.
Signed with our hand’s signatures, from Dan to Beth-el,
Elders of the state council on the land of Ariel.
The city, town of Tel Aviv, in our birth land,
1948, return by our count,
May quartodeciman, fifth of Iyar, the day before our rest.
Let us merit to read this scroll on our independence day!
Silluq
And thus, to You holiness ascends,
For You are the Holy One and Savior of Israel.
On the third seventh of the seven weeks,
Between stress and distress to establishing salvation,
Good amazing news was heard:
The lonely one will teem with people when breaches breach.
In days of renewal, in set seasons,
The coming of independence, for the hours have come.
My Creator, the wonders You have done are known!
From people to people the land was handed over;
Tyrants of the channels that none would idolize.
They rose in conquest but fell in the breach.
And the Canaanite and Perizzite were then settled in the land.
The father went up from Sumer, his son abode there,
And the sons of his pure son went down to save their lives.
In the days of their enslavement they cried out from their abuse.
Those born of Jochebed arose to bring them up from there,
For Canaan had sinned beyond a guilt-offering’s rectification.
And the free ones ascended to acquire their inheritance.
The land was apportioned to twelve tribes,
And in those days, the days the judges judged,
There was no king in Israel to do judgment.
They besought the Mizpatite, and their words were received.
The Benjaminite and his psalmist reigned over the people
And the wise secret-knower who build the pleasant house,
After that, vinegar son of wine, Rehoboam,
And from Ephraim rose the sinner and sin-causer Jeroboam,
And the northerners rebelled and split the people;
ten left this time,
and with the casting of the double-calves the gold was dimmed.
Assyria took those neglectful of the Surveyor
And settled them in Halah, Khabur, Guzana, and Media,
But Jerusalem, the house of my learning,
Was not conquered by his hand, due to a legitimate plague.
Pul’s disease was more than enough for him
But Judah sinned in the reign of Manasseh,
And forgot the teaching given by Moses’ hand,
And Sheshakh Lev-Qamai came, and a hard day,
Until Cyrus announced, “you will forget your exile!”
Persia ruled over us year after year,
Till Alexander of Macedon came upon the lilies.
He died, and his kingdom was divided among four chiefs,
And Coele-Syria to Seleucus and his stubborn sons,
Among them Antiochus, desecrator of holy things.
He was called mad, his fruits rotten.
Against him rose heroes of men,
The Hasmoneans who kindled fires.
But generations descended in the way of man,
There was strife between the Sadducee and Pharisee guides.
Until the children of Jannaeus reigned, such fools,
Who invited Rome to intercede in punishments.
It acquired our land to be acquisitions,
And what they acquire they do not abandon.
They raised Herod and did conquering,
And when the zealous and stubborn ones battled,
They destroyed our Temple and we were expelled.
Your song in a foreign land sounds like such noise!
And a new image rose over them, from my people’s children,
But it did not help us, for the image was Rome’s.
After hundreds of years rose my blood’s avenger,
Omar, over Ishmael, conquerer of the Jerusalemite.
He opened for me gates and sought my peace.
But where is the prince who will come out from me?
And where is the ruler, from where is he found?
Independence is the matter that Israel wants!
From a barbarous land arose the crusaders,
Low men, murderers and hateful.
Blood spilt up to the ankle on the floor of the palaces.
Are these your heroes, murderers of the faithful?
In the end they were conquered, no forgiveness for the laws.
After this the Turks conquered it.
Their king, named wisely, renewed the wall.
War arose between all the nations.
The Turks chose the losing side to disgrace.
The Brits entered with a mandate for its nation.
Balfour declared that the land would be given to its people.
But every regime is hypocritical — who knows why?
And the white paper doomed millions of the nation.
When the foul desolation was revealed to all
That the mockers perpetrated upon the uncomforted,
The assembly of uniting every nation
Declared that no longer would we be utterly persecuted.
And thus, come, let us sing a song of thanks.
For salvation They were to me, my strength and song, Yah!
And in every city and kibbutz and settlement and town
Let us hymn with the ministers of Akhtriel Yah,
Snake- and mount- and wheel- and beast-angel,
Those singing always and the creation-renewed,
Those dwelling above and below praise Yah,
And the holy Trisagion is the reading.
Announce, all, aloud, halleluyah!
As written by Your prophet’s hand,
and they called one to another and said... (Isaiah 6:3).

While the honey in the phrase “flowing with milk and honey” is generally said to refer to date honey, or silan, bee honey is unique in that it the only product of a non-kosher animal that is kosher. (Bavli Bekhorot 7b).

The notorious lost Legio IX Hispana, it has been suggested, was destroyed in the Bar Kokhba rebellion. While the fate of Legio IX Hispana is uncertain, another legion, Legio XXII Deiotariana was last recorded in an ignomious defeat at the hands of Bar Kokhba’s forces, and seems to have been disbanded soon afterwards.

Still eaten in Israel today, this fish Sarpa salpa, also known as the salema porgy, the cow bream, or the dreamfish, is notorious for, in some rare cases, causing hallucinations when its entrails are consumed.
In modern Hebrew this word for a fish is used to describe salmon, which is almost certainly not what is ntended in the Mishnah where it is stated to live off the Egyptian coast.
A name for the sabbath between Yom haShoah and Yom ha-Atsma’ut, which the author first came across in the new Tefilat haAdam Israeli Reform siddur.

This reshut, introducing the poetic retelling of the Scroll of Independence, is largely a justification of the custom of celebrating Yom ha-Atsma’ut. It lists other examples of Jews adding new holidays or celebrating secular days as religious days.
Meaning the third day of the three days of Yom haShoah, Yom haZikaron, and Yom ha-Atsma’ut.
As in Ḥanukkah, which, like Yom ha-Atsma’ut, is a day of celebrating independence in the land.
